text:
incident-bot: Pager: high org qps spike detected for org=brightline (95th qps 4.8x baseline). Routing errors up, some 502s from rider-service. Paging @mike_oncall.

mike_oncall: I’m on it. Seeing a big jump in prefix cache misses + open connections. Do we have a mapped campaign?

ella_support: Brightline support reported sudden traffic from a promo email they sent ~10m ago. They say it's expected but bursty.

alex_sre: Confirmed spike hitting inference-proxy in us-west-2. Per-org throttles are firing but their burst token pool exhausted. We should apply a temporary org override to avoid user-visible 502s. Thoughts on duration?

mike_oncall: +1 for an override. Keep short: 30m then reassess. We should also disable streaming responses for that org — streaming is amplifying connections.

jamal_devex: I can run the override. Suggested CLI: 
```
infractl org rate override --org brightline --max-qps 1200 --tokens-per-minute 180000 --expires 2026-03-17T15:10:00Z --reason "promo burst mitigation"
```
Will that work?

alex_sre: That looks good. Also add a route rule to downgrade them to the cheaper model variant if latency spikes: addRule(org=brightline, fallback_model=fast-small, priority=50).

mike_oncall: Execute both. Jamal, do the rate override. Alex, push the routing rule. Ella, tell Brightline support about the temporary changes and ask for ETA on campaign traffic.

jamal_devex: Running override now. 
```
$ infractl org rate override --org brightline --max-qps 1200 --tokens-per-minute 180000 --expires 2026-03-17T15:10:00Z --reason "promo burst mitigation"
Applied override id=ovr_9c7f2a, effective=now, expires=2026-03-17T15:10:00Z
```

alex_sre: Pushed routing rule and set fallback threshold to 250ms p95. Rule id=rout_33a. Verified in staging and promoted.

incident-bot: System: org override ovr_9c7f2a active for brightline. Routing rule rout_33a active.

mike_oncall: Metrics look better — 502s down to baseline, latency slightly higher but within SLO. Streaming disabled via toggle for org brightline (toggle id=feat_stream_disable_784).

ella_support: Notified Brightline: "We've applied a temporary rate override and disabled streaming for 30m to protect customer traffic; monitoring closely. Please let us know when the campaign ends." They replied: "thanks, will update if more traffic."

jamal_devex: Leaving a short runbook note: 
- override id=ovr_9c7f2a (expires 2026-03-17T15:10Z)
- routing rule rout_33a (fallback -> fast-small)
- disabled feature feat_stream_disable_784 for org brightline
- suggested follow-up: confirm campaign end & gradually revert override

mike_oncall: Will monitor for the next 30m. If traffic persists after expiry, we’ll coordinate a longer mitigation or engage account lead for quota lift. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

alex_sre: Post-incident action: create an automated policy to detect promo-like bursts (pattern: sudden 3x qps increase + SMTP-triggered events) and suggest org override playbook. Filing ticket now.

incident-bot: Thread closed. If anything changes, reopen or @mike_oncall to page on-call."
